rows.title: Where to stop
rows.text: About 150,000 CLP is the knee of the curve: Toph's tutor package is the cheapest big jump (7.1 to 7.4 for about 49,000 CLP), while Azula and Ezio already sit near their ceiling from about 46,000 to 50,000 CLP each. Going further buys little, so spend more only on a deck that is still climbing.

rows.title: Buy order inside a deck
rows.text: 1) the cheap untapped dual lands and signets of the three-color and five-color decks (Azula, Ezio, then Toph): they fix the mana base for a few thousand CLP. 2) Tutors that reach the win lines (Toph: Reckless Handling, Brightglass Gearhulk, Chord of Calling). 3) Fast cheap pieces. 4) Expensive staples last: they did not move Commander Salt's power.

rows.title: What decides the game
rows.text: All three decks play the same way: a cheap engine that makes the commander matter by turn 3 or 4, tutors that find one of two or three late-game win lines, and a few cheap answers. Keep the answers for the one permanent that stops your line, not for the first threat you see.

rows.title: Idea
rows.text: Landfall deck built on Toph's rule: every nontoken artifact you control is also a land. Each rock, locket or bauble is therefore a land drop that triggers landfall, and at your end step Toph earthbends 2 (a land becomes a haste creature with two +1/+1 counters that returns if it dies). Landfall pingers (Tannuk, Sabotender, Ragost, Valakut Exploration) drain the table while cheap ramp and tutors keep the engine fed.

rows.title: Fair win
rows.text: Most games end by damage: Sabotender and Tannuk hit every opponent for each land, Valakut Exploration turns the exiled cards into damage at your end step, and Bumi, Unleashed (earthbend 4, trample) untaps your lands whenever he connects.

rows.title: Line A: Bumi and Coating
rows.text: Toph + Bumi, Unleashed + Liquimetal Coating. Coating makes Bumi an artifact, so under Toph a land. When Bumi connects all your lands untap and there is another combat in which only land creatures attack, so he attacks again and again. Rogue's Passage keeps him unblockable.

rows.title: Line B: Ashaya and Bumi
rows.text: Ashaya makes every nontoken creature a Forest land, so Bumi is a land without Coating and loops the same way. It is a two-card line that needs about ten mana, so it is a late-game finish.

rows.title: Line C: Ashaya, Zuran Orb and a pinger
rows.text: Ashaya + Zuran Orb + a creature that earthbends when it enters (Toph the Blind Bandit, Earth Kingdom General): the creature is a land, sacrifices itself to the Orb, returns and earthbends itself again, for infinite enters, landfall and deaths. Goblin Bombardment wins on its own; Sylvan Safekeeper or any landfall pinger also finish.

rows.title: Line D: infinite landfall
rows.text: Toph + Springheart Nantuko + Lotus Cobra or Tireless Provisioner: three cards with two-mana pieces make infinite landfall, and any pinger or Valakut Exploration is lethal. It is the fastest line of the deck.

rows.title: Tutors
rows.text: Seismic Sense and Crop Rotation from the free base, then Reckless Handling (finds Coating, Torque, Zuran Orb), Brightglass Gearhulk, Chord of Calling (any creature, convoked by earthbent lands), and later Imperial Recruiter, Inventors' Fair, Gamble and more. Whichever piece is missing, something finds it.

rows.title: How it plays
rows.text: Turns 1 and 2: Sol Ring, signets, talismans, Wayfarer's Bauble, Sakura-Tribe Elder or Lotus Cobra. Turn 3 or 4: Toph, as soon as you control two artifacts to turn into lands; from then on every artifact is a land drop. Keep Swords, Path, Beast Within and Fateful Absence for the permanent that stops your line, and protect Toph with The Stasis Coffin or Redirect Lightning.

rows.title: Watch out
rows.text: Bumi must connect in the first combat, and Liquimetal Coating only lasts until end of turn. Ashaya's creatures are still summoning sick for tap abilities. Gamble discards a card at random after the search, so cast it with a full hand or as your last card. Brightglass Gearhulk puts the two cards into your hand, not onto the battlefield. Artifact removal and sweepers hit your land-artifacts.

rows.title: Idea
rows.text: Grixis combat spellslinger. Fire Lord Azula attacks every turn: firebending adds {R}{R} when she attacks, and every spell you cast while she is attacking is copied. So the best cards are cheap instants: removal, card draw and Treasure makers become two-for-ones, and a few cost reducers make them nearly free.

rows.title: Engine
rows.text: Goblin Electromancer, Stormcatch Mentor and Nightscape Familiar reduce the cost of your spells; Electro adds red mana for each instant and sorcery, Storm-Kiln Artist makes a Treasure for each one, Archmage Emeritus draws, and Guttersnipe and Black Waltz No. 3 hit every opponent for each noncreature spell. Cheap duals let her come down on curve and still hold mana for combat.

rows.title: Loops
rows.text: Azula + Narset's Reversal + Frantic Search, or + Storm-Kiln Artist; Snap + Dualcaster Mage; Dualcaster Mage + Ember Island Production. Each loop gives unlimited casts while she attacks, and Guttersnipe, Black Waltz No. 3, Electro or a big X spell closes it. Mystical Teachings (copied, both halves) finds the instants.

rows.title: Copied X spells
rows.text: Comet Storm, Electrodominance, Exsanguinate and Invoke Calamity cast while she attacks are copied: Treasures, rituals and Electro's mana pay for a large X.

rows.title: Commander damage
rows.text: Bulk Up on an attacking Azula is copied, so her power doubles twice; its flashback, also copied, doubles it twice more. A single combat can kill by commander damage.

rows.title: How it plays
rows.text: Keep two or three lands, a cost reducer and cheap instants. Cast Azula on turn 4 with Swiftfoot Boots, Deflecting Swat or Redirect behind her, attack every turn and cast your instants during combat so each is copied. Use removal on the blockers or the threat, draw spells to dig for the loop.

rows.title: Watch out
rows.text: Archmage Emeritus draws are mandatory, so stop a loop before you deck yourself. Ritual mana empties between combat steps unless Electro, Ozai or The Last Agni Kai keeps it. Sorceries and creatures are copied only if they have flash. Ember Island Production can copy Azula as a non-legendary token, so two attacking Azulas copy every spell twice.

rows.title: Weak spots
rows.text: She has to survive to attack: instant-speed removal or a wall of blockers slows the plan. Commander Salt caps her because the combo wincons have few tutors to assemble them, which is exactly what the next round of lists attacks.

rows.title: Idea
rows.text: Five-color Assassin tempo with black at the core. Ezio is a two-mana menace attacker: once he or any Assassin connects, Assassin spells cost {B}{B} (freerunning). Roshan, Hidden Magister makes every creature an Assassin, so the whole deck gets the discount; Brotherhood Headquarters pays for them, and Ezio, Blade of Vengeance draws a card each time an Assassin connects.

rows.title: Ezio's own win
rows.text: If Ezio connects while a player has 10 life or less, pay {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} and that player loses the game. Whispersilk Cloak, Secret Tunnel or Assassin Gauntlet (which taps their creatures) make him unblockable; card draw from combat and the monarch keeps the pressure up.

rows.title: Line A: Godo and Helm of the Host
rows.text: Godo, Bandit Warlord puts Helm of the Host onto the battlefield when he enters. Equip Helm to Godo for {5}: at each combat a hasty token copy of Godo is made, it attacks for the first time, untaps and adds another combat, for infinite combats.

rows.title: Line B: Kiki-Jiki
rows.text: Kiki-Jiki + Intruder Alarm gives infinite hasty tokens at any time, and Kiki-Jiki + Helm of the Host + Goblin Bombardment turns the loop into damage. They are late-game backups to Line A.

rows.title: Tutors
rows.text: Godo finds Helm; Loyal Inventor and Reckless Handling find Helm too; Entomb followed by Restart Sequence or What Must Be Done reanimates Godo; Seismic Sense and Gamble reach the rest.

rows.title: How it plays
rows.text: Turn 2 Ezio, attack with menace. After a hit, cast the freerunning spells (Eagle Vision, Chain Assassination, Restart Sequence) for {B}{B}, and Roshan or a cheap Assassin follows. Thorn of the Black Rose and Queen Marchesa make you the monarch for card flow; Murder, Terminate, Counterspell and Fact or Fiction keep the table honest while the Assassins connect.

rows.title: Watch out
rows.text: Five colors on few basics: the cheap untapped duals are the first purchase. Ezio is a two-mana creature, so keep Swiftfoot Boots or removal mana ready to protect him; creature sweepers hurt the whole plan. The commander is a proxy at no cost; the real card is an optional purchase outside the budget.

rows.title: Where he ended
rows.text: Alexios, Deimos of Kosmos is a four-mana mono red commander that attacks each combat and passes to the next player's control at every upkeep, so the deck is a political chaos engine. His measured ladder scored below Ezio at every price on Commander Salt (see the power chart), so Ezio takes the new-deck slot. Alexios' files stay in the repository until you confirm the replacement.
